name: Repurpose.io
tagline: Automatically reformats and publishes audio and video across platforms

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Up to 3 accounts per social network; 5,000 published videos/month

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Up to 10 accounts per social network; unlimited published videos

tiers.name: Agency
tiers.limits: Up to 25 accounts per social network; unlimited published videos

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual page labels save 17%); 14-day trial or 10 published audios/videos, whichever comes first; no card required
pricing.hiddenCosts: Trial ends at the earlier of 14 days or 10 published audios/videos; account caps apply separately to each social network; no public overage rate.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Repurpose.io's durable value is platform APIs, distribution, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a personal content repurposing planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: official platform OAuth credentials where available
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: protection from API and policy changes
production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates
whyPeopleStillPay: Repurpose.io: Social tools survive because networks change APIs, permissions, formats, and anti-spam rules constantly.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, token refresh, media constraints, rate limits, scheduling, webhooks, retries, and platform policy compliance.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social scheduling and publishing platform.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: You can resize and edit formats manually, which is precisely the labour Repurpose.io sells away.

rejectedAlternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A destination scheduler, not an automatic media-reformatting pipeline.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Postiz
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It publishes existing media; it does not automatically transcode and reframe audio or video for every network.

notes: Credibility row: Repurpose.io survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Repurpose.io; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + BullMQ.
Primary job: Build a personal content repurposing planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: team approvals and asset workflows; protection from API and policy changes; production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
